99DOTS digital adherence stepped-wedge trial, Uganda (Cattamanchi et al. 2021)

Source: R/data.R
dots99.Rd

Patient-level public data of the 99DOTS stepped-wedge trial: 18 health facilities in six randomisation blocks, eight trial months, treatment success as the primary outcome. Used by Halkiewicz and Alexeev (arXiv:2610.35853) as the application with no detectable heterogeneity but low power to rule out heterogeneity that would damage IT inference.

Usage

dots99

Format

A data frame with 2,224 rows and 13 variables:

block

intervention group (randomisation block 1–6)

facility

health facility 1–18 (cluster)

facility_type

facility type

month

trial month 0–7

period

study period: Control, Buffer, or Intervention

sex, age, hiv, disease_class, retreatment

patient characteristics

treated_successfully, persisting, not_ltfu

outcomes (Yes/No)

Source

Cattamanchi A, Crowder R, Kityamuwesi A, et al. (2021). Digital adherence technology for tuberculosis treatment supervision: a stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial in Uganda. PLOS Medicine 18(5): e1003628, doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.1003628 ; S1 Data, doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.1003628.s002 . Licence: CC BY 4.0 (not covered by the package's MIT licence). Column names are snake_case; commas inside text labels are replaced by semicolons. See inst/DATA_SOURCES.md.

Examples

table(dots99$block, dots99$period)
#>    
#>     Buffer period Control Intervention
#>   1            47      30          192
#>   2            33      56          164
#>   3            64     150          231
#>   4            36     148          116
#>   5            69     303          136
#>   6            62     335           52
